newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea news agency to debut on Internet this week.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea news agency to debut on Internet this week.

text.p: North Korea, one of the world's most reclusive nations, will open its first site on the World Wide Web on Thursday, its Japanese distributors said on Monday.

Dispatches in English from the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) will be available to all Internet users, an official from the Korea News Service, which acts as Japanese agent for the Pyongyang news agency, told Reuters.
The Korea News Service distributes news about North Korea to pro-Pyongyang Korean residents in Japan.

"Up to 18 news items will be available on the Internet each day," the official said. "By opening the Internet page, we would like to disseminate news from the DPRK (North Korea) more widely throughout the world."
Last month, authorities in South Korea warned Internet providers there that they risked lengthy jail terms if they distributed Pyongyang propaganda.
South Korea bans the distribution of any information or material benefiting North Korea and violators can be jailed for up to seven years.
North and South Korea have remained technically at war since their 1950-53 conflict ended with a truce.
KCNA is regarded as the official voice of North Korea and the communist nation often makes important announcements through the news agency.
On December 29, for example, Pyongyang issued a statement through KCNA that apologised for the first time for an incursion by one of its submarines into South Korea in September.

South Korea blocked access to a Canadian-based Internet service provider last year after a Canadian student opened a page carrying North Korean propaganda. It lifted the restriction after the page was closed.
